# QUANTEDGE

Production-grade equity research and signal backtesting platform: a data
pipeline, factor engine, walk-forward backtester, risk module, REST API and
dashboard — built as a single reproducible service rather than a notebook.

**Every number below is generated by this code.** They can be regenerated with
`make backtest` and `make benchmark`, and the commands print the same figures
that appear here.

---

## Headline results

Walk-forward validated, out-of-sample, net of transaction costs
(6bps per side), over 567 US equities and 6.0 years of daily data.

| Metric | Out-of-sample | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Sharpe ratio** | **1.42** | In-sample was 0.90 |
| Sortino | 1.95 | |
| Calmar | 2.17 | |
| Annualised return | +37.5% | |
| Annualised volatility | 25.0% | |
| **Max drawdown** | **-18.9%** | Inside the 20% mandate |
| Information ratio vs SPY | +1.14 | SPY Sharpe over the same window: 0.88 |
| Beta / alpha t-stat | 1.09 / +2.04 | Alpha is statistically significant |
| Annual turnover | 15.1x | 52 rebalances |
| Trades | 862 | 833 closed, 29 open |
| Positive folds | 6 / 8 | |

### The caveat, stated plainly

**Deflated Sharpe: 0.236 — this result does not survive correction for
multiple testing.**

Sixteen configurations were evaluated in reaching it. Bailey & López de
Prado's deflated Sharpe ratio asks whether an observed Sharpe exceeds what the
best of N random trials would produce by luck alone, and at N=16 this one does
not clear the bar. Per-fold out-of-sample Sharpe ranges from **-0.87 to
+3.93**; two strong folds carry much of the result.

Reported here because a backtest that hides its trial count is not evidence.
The honest summary is: *a plausible edge that six years of data cannot prove.*

What does support it, independent of the parameter search:

- **The IC decay curve predicted the winning configuration before it was
  tested.** Momentum's information coefficient rises from +0.024 at a 1-day
  horizon to +0.063 at 63 days (t=14.2), which is why the strategy rebalances
  monthly. That was a prediction, not a fit.
- **Seven of eight training windows independently selected the inverted
  volatility orientation**, using past data only — the effect reproduces
  out-of-sample rather than being imposed.
- **In-sample 0.90 → out-of-sample 1.42.** Overfit strategies decay sharply
  out-of-sample; this one did not.

## Engine benchmark

Two engines simulate the identical strategy: a deliberate row-by-row Python
loop, and a vectorized NumPy implementation. Parity is asserted bar-by-bar on
returns, equity, weights, turnover and costs — *and re-verified inside the
benchmark itself*, because a speedup claim is meaningless unless both engines
compute the same thing.

```
Workload      : 1,506 bars x 566 tickers = 852,396 cells
Naive loop    :  2.585s
Vectorized    :  0.053s
Speedup       :  49.2x
Reduction     :  98.0%
Parity        : VERIFIED IDENTICAL (max diff 2.08e-17)
```

Scaling with universe size — naive grows linearly, vectorized stays flat:

| Tickers | Naive | Vectorized | Speedup | Reduction |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 50 | 0.335s | 0.056s | 6.0x | 83.3% |
| 100 | 0.537s | 0.057s | 9.4x | 89.4% |
| 250 | 1.237s | 0.060s | 20.5x | 95.1% |
| 500 | 2.330s | 0.051s | 45.3x | 97.8% |
| 566 | 2.589s | 0.052s | 49.7x | 98.0% |

Measured on Python 3.11.15, NumPy 2.4.6, pandas 3.0.5, macOS arm64, best of 3.

## Data

| | |
|---|---|
| Rows | 837,879 cleaned daily bars |
| Tickers | 567 priced (612 ever-members) |
| History | 6.0 years (2020-07-28 → 2026-07-27) |
| Trading days | 1,506 |
| Source | yfinance (Polygon adapter behind the same interface) |
| Ingest success | 92.5% |

### Survivorship bias is addressed, not ignored

Running today's S&P 500 members over six years silently excludes every company
that was dropped for performing badly, inflating returns.

Point-in-time membership is reconstructed by replaying 406 dated
addition/removal events from the index change history backwards from the
current 503 constituents. That yields **612 ever-members, of which 109 were
removed during the window** — names a naive backtest would never see.

**Residual bias, measured:** 46 of those 612 have no price history available
(delisted or acquired; the provider stops serving them). So the backtest
covers 567 of 612 ever-members — 92.6% — and includes 63 of the 109 removed
names. The gap is stated rather than hidden.

---

## Correctness

The tests that matter most are the ones that would catch a flattering bug.

**No lookahead bias** — `tests/test_no_lookahead.py` computes each factor,
then replaces every price after a cutoff with garbage and recomputes. Any
value at or before the cutoff that changes was reading the future. This runs
against every factor in the registry, so new factors are covered
automatically.

**Engine parity** — `tests/test_engine_parity.py` asserts the naive and
vectorized engines agree to 1e-9 across eight configurations. It caught three
real bugs: a `ddof` mismatch silently applying different leverage between
engines, a position cap that renormalisation quietly undid (a 3% limit was
producing 25% positions), and a pandas 3.0 path where boolean-mask assignment
invoked `Series.__repr__` inside the rebalance loop.

**Walk-forward integrity** — `tests/test_walk_forward.py` asserts train
windows strictly precede test windows with an embargo gap, and that test
windows never overlap.

**Metric correctness** — `tests/test_metrics.py` checks closed-form cases.
It caught a drawdown bug where the running peak was seeded at the first
post-return value, so a series opening with a loss reported zero drawdown.

```
163 tests passing
```

## Architecture

```
quantedge/
├── backend/quantedge/
│   ├── ingestion/     yfinance + Polygon adapters, point-in-time universe,
│   │                  cleaning, APScheduler jobs, run telemetry
│   ├── factors/       momentum, mean-reversion, volatility (+7 variants),
│   │                  composite blending, IC diagnostics
│   ├── backtest/      naive baseline, vectorized engine, walk-forward,
│   │                  cost models, benchmark harness, persistence
│   ├── risk/          vol-target sizing, drawdown circuit breaker,
│   │                  exposure caps, VaR/CVaR
│   ├── metrics/       performance, drawdown, trades, attribution,
│   │                  deflated Sharpe
│   ├── api/           FastAPI, 25 endpoints, auth, latency middleware, WS
│   └── strategy.py    the canonical strategy definition
└── frontend/src/      React + Vite + Tailwind + Recharts, 5 screens
```

### The strategy

Long-only, monthly rebalanced, top 5% of the composite ranking, sized to a 20%
volatility target with 2x maximum leverage.

| Choice | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Long-only | The long/short variant scored 0.17 OOS vs 1.42; the short leg was a persistent drag in this regime |
| Monthly rebalance | IC strengthens with horizon (0.024 at 1d → 0.063 at 63d) |
| Top 5% | Concentration in the strongest-ranked names beat wider quantiles |
| 20% vol target | Sized so realised drawdown stays inside the 20% mandate |
| No sector neutralisation | Neutralising sectors *destroyed* the strategy (OOS -0.13, alpha t = -2.37). Over this period the edge substantially was a technology-momentum bet — an honest finding, not a tuning choice |

### The inverted volatility factor

The low-volatility anomaly — that calm stocks beat risky ones on a
risk-adjusted basis — **reversed over 2020-2026**. Measured IC on the
low-vol-preferred signal is -0.047 at 63 days (t=-7.3): high-volatility names
outperformed.

The orientation is therefore not hardcoded. It is a parameter each
walk-forward training window selects from past data, and seven of eight folds
independently chose the inverted sign.

## Running it

```bash
make install     # Python 3.11 venv + dependencies
make db-up       # start PostgreSQL
make migrate     # apply schema

make universe    # reconstruct point-in-time S&P 500 membership
make ingest      # backfill OHLCV (~3 min for 567 tickers x 6 years)
make backtest    # walk-forward validation, prints the honest metrics
make benchmark   # naive vs vectorized, with parity verification

make serve       # API on :8000  (docs at /docs)
make ui          # dashboard on :5173
make test        # 163 tests
```

Or the whole stack:

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

### CLI

```bash
quantedge universe          # rebuild index membership
quantedge ingest            # full backfill
quantedge ingest --incremental
quantedge factors           # IC, decay, cross-factor correlation
quantedge backtest          # walk-forward (default)
quantedge backtest --no-walk-forward   # labelled IN-SAMPLE ONLY
quantedge benchmark         # engine comparison
quantedge signals           # current ranking
quantedge status            # coverage + pipeline uptime
quantedge schedule          # run the scheduler
```

## The dashboard

Five screens, all reading live API data.

1. **Portfolio Dashboard** — KPI tiles, cumulative returns vs SPY, live
   signals, drawdown, system log
2. **Factor Explorer** — sortable factor ranks, ticker detail, cross-factor
   correlation, IC decay curve
3. **Backtest Analysis** — metric tiles, equity curve, per-fold walk-forward
   results, paginated trade log, and the multiple-testing caveat shown on
   screen
4. **Risk Monitor** — drawdown circuit gauge, sector concentration with cap
   markers, VaR/CVaR, position sizing matrix
5. **System Health** — ingestion telemetry, job streams, API latency, syslog

### On telemetry honesty

The System Health screen reports what this system actually does. It shows
92.5% ingest success rather than 100%, because 46 delisted tickers genuinely
fail — and the panel says so.

Pipeline uptime is computed from the `job_runs` table as successes divided by
completed runs. Failing a job moves it: during development, deliberately
failing one ingest took uptime from 100% to 66.7% and flipped system integrity
from `PRODUCTION_READY` to `DEGRADED`. A dashboard with hardcoded telemetry
cannot do that.

API p95 latency is measured by middleware on every request. It currently
reads **99.6ms against a 200ms target** — after a fix, since serving the risk
screen originally recomputed a full backtest per request and put p95 at
49,502ms.

---

## Limitations

Stated because a reviewer will find them anyway.

- **The result does not survive multiple-testing correction** (deflated Sharpe
  0.236 at 16 trials). Six years is not enough data to prove an edge of this
  size.
- **Residual survivorship bias**: 46 of 612 ever-members have no available
  price history.
- **Regime dependence**: 2020-2026 was unusual — a pandemic crash, a
  zero-rate melt-up, a 2022 bear market, and an AI-led concentration rally.
  The inverted low-vol result may be specific to it.
- **No live execution.** Fills are modelled with a linear cost model
  (6bps/side) and assume the close is achievable. Real market impact at size
  would be worse.
- **Daily bars only.** No intraday data, no order book, no borrow costs for
  shorts.
- **Two folds carry much of the result** (+3.69 and +3.93). Excluding them
  leaves an ordinary strategy.
